text:
Maya: Heads-up: my FastAPI sample app using py-sdk v0.9.7 isn't linking traces to startup/background tasks. Logs show request-id missing for background infer calls. Anyone seen this with the new observability hooks?

Jordan: Hmm can you paste a minimal repro? Are you using sdk.install_observability_hooks or the middleware from the docs?

Maya: Wired the hooks like docs: client = RedwoodClient(...); client.install_observability_hooks(). In the handler I do an await and also fire-and-forget a background generate with create_task. The background span shows up as a root span, not a child of the incoming request. Also the logs for the background task lack the request-id.

Sam: That sounds like contextvars loss across create_task. Async context propagation doesn't automatically carry over in a couple of spawn patterns. Are you on uvloop or using any custom executors?

Maya: Using uvicorn + uvloop, Python 3.11. Minimal snippet: 
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(...)
client.install_observability_hooks()
@app.post("/run")
async def run(req: Request):
    resp = await client.generate(prompt)
    asyncio.create_task(client.generate_asyncfire(prompt))  # background call
    return resp
```
Second call has no traceparent header and no request-id in logs.

Lee: I think our instrumentation added header injection for direct request paths but we missed capturing context when we spawn background tasks or when the retry layer creates a fresh httpx client. Two quick workarounds: 1) copy the context when creating the task (contextvars.copy_context) or 2) manually inject propagated headers into the background call. We should still patch the SDK to capture context for its internal async work.

Jordan: Try this quick test — wrap the spawn: 
```python
import contextvars, asyncio
ctx = contextvars.copy_context()
asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(ctx.run(client.generate_asyncfire, prompt))
```
If that preserves the traceparent then it's a context-capture bug in the SDK.

Maya: Will try now. Also saw retry middleware re-sending requests without our tracing headers on 429s when using client.retry_async, so feels like two places (task spawn + retry path).

Sam: Historically the async retry code created a new AsyncClient per attempt and didn't copy over custom headers from the original request. I'll add a fix to preserve headers across retries and to ensure propagators are used for each attempt.

Maya: Filed a repro issue with snippet and logs: https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/478 (contains minimal app and failing trace screenshot).

deploy-bot: Published release 0.9.8-rc1 with an observability fix candidate: "preserve async context for spawned tasks" (changelog: https://github.com/redwood/repo/releases/tag/v0.9.8-rc1) :tada:

Jordan: Nice — can someone add an integration test: FastAPI handler -> background task -> retry path -> OTLP export should show a single trace with 2 or 3 spans? That will catch regressions.

Lee: I'll add the test + update the sample app in docs to show the recommended pattern (either use contextvars.copy_context or the SDK helper we plan to expose like client.spawn_with_context). Also add a note in the observability page about middleware ordering (install hooks before auth/retry wiring).

Maya: Thanks — I'll test rc and report back on the issue. :thumbsup:
